newsitem.title: USA: Alaska governor to lead oil trade mission to Sakhalin.
newsitem.headline: Alaska governor to lead oil trade mission to Sakhalin.

text.p: Alaska Gov. Tony Knowles said Saturday he will lead an oil and gas trade mission to the Russia's Sakhalin Island, site of an embryonic industry boom.
In a speech to the Alaska Support Industry Alliance annual conference, Knowles also said he has appointed an Alaska representative to work in Sakhalin.

"The enormous oil and gas reserves around Sakhalin are going to be developed in coming years, so it only makes good business sense that Alaskans get in on the ground floor," Knowles, a Democrat, told the gathering of oil-field service company officials.

"Alaskans are world leaders in cold weather oil and gas development and our expertise is needed in the Russian Far East. My trade mission and having an official state representative on Sakhalin should help open important doors for Alaskan companies," he said.

The Alaska representative will be Dinty Miller, a former Alaskan who serves as executive director of the American Business Center on the Russian island. The center, financed mostly by the federal government, promotes U.S.-Russian ties, Knowles said.

Sakhalin is the site of four major oil and gas projects involving several oil companies, including Exxon and Marathon Oil. Several Alaska oil-field survice companies have sought contracts on development projects on the Russian island.
Alaska Commerce Commissioner Willie Hensley said the date of the governor's trade mission has not been set, but that it will occur in the next couple of months.
Knowles visited Sakhalin two years ago when he delivered medical equipment and other relief suppolies after a devastating earthquake on the island's northern tip.
